resources.string: Aortic root and arch
Aortic cutaway · Front view, body right at image left
Aortic valve
The pale cusps mark the boundary between the left ventricular outflow and the aortic root. They open toward the aorta.
Aortic sinus
This pocket immediately above a valve cusp is one of the three aortic sinuses. The right and left coronary arteries begin in two of these sinuses.
Ascending aorta
Above the widened root, this segment rises from the sinotubular junction to the first arch branch, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle.
Aortic arch
The arch turns backward and toward the left side of the body. The three usual branches leave its upper curve in the order shown.
Brachiocephalic trunk
The first arch branch heads to the right and divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries beyond this view.
Left common carotid
The second arch branch rises toward the left side of the neck and carries blood toward the head and neck.
Left subclavian
The third arch branch turns toward the left shoulder and carries blood toward the left upper limb.
Descending aorta
Beyond the left subclavian origin, the arch turns down into the descending thoracic aorta behind the heart.
Pulmonary trunk bifurcation
Pulmonary outflow cutaway · Front view, body right at image left
Pulmonary valve
The pale cusps sit between the right ventricular outflow and the base of the pulmonary trunk. They open toward the trunk.
Pulmonary trunk
This short blue vessel rises from the right ventricle, in front of and then to the left of the ascending aorta. Blue denotes oxygen-poor blood headed to the lungs.
Bifurcation
Just beneath the aortic arch, the pulmonary trunk splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries, one to each lung.
Right pulmonary artery
The longer branch runs toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta. The muted red aorta is partly transparent to reveal that crossing.
Left pulmonary artery
The shorter branch passes in front of the descending aorta and above the left main bronchus on its way to the left lung.
Epicardial coronary routes
Coronary surface cutaway · Front view, body right at image left
Right coronary artery
From the right aortic sinus, this red artery tracks between the right atrium and right ventricle in the right atrioventricular groove. The red routes carry oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle.
Right marginal branch
This branch leaves the right coronary artery at the lower right border of the heart and runs toward the apex along the right ventricular surface.
Left main coronary

The short stem starts at the left aortic sinus, passes between the pulmonary trunk and left atrial appendage, then divides into the LAD and circumflex. The overlying trunk is muted to expose the origin.
LAD
The left anterior descending artery runs toward the apex in the anterior interventricular groove, between the right and left ventricles.
Circumflex artery
From the left main division, the circumflex follows the left atrioventricular groove between the left atrium and left ventricle, then wraps out of view.
